newsitem.title: INDIA: India's cyclone-hit state seeks aid for crops.
newsitem.headline: India's cyclone-hit state seeks aid for crops.

text.p: The Indian state of Andhra Pradesh is seeking around one billion rupees ($30 million) in compensation for coconut farmers whose trees were destroyed in last week's cyclone, a senior government official said on Friday.
Agriculture Minister S.V. Subba Reddy said as many as five million coconut trees are estimated to have been damaged by the cyclone that lashed the southeast coast on November 6.
Reddy said the Coconut Board had recommended that the central government pay 200 rupees per tree to affected farmers.
State Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu on Thursday criticised the central government for not releasing enough resources quickly to help Andhra Pradesh deal with the disaster.
Naidu also said on Thursday that 847 people were killed by the cyclone while 925 more were still missing.
An updated death toll was not made available on Friday.
The Indian Red Cross said hundreds of people in outlying villages were still cut off by flood waters created by the cyclone's torrential rains and sea water driven in by 180-kph (110-mph) winds.
